crossplot: A least-squares line of y on x where both have values: first the zone level (each zone's means: their rank correlation across the zones in words, and the line through them), then each zone, the zones pooled, and the whole interval where samples outside the zones add to it: n of N, slope (y per unit of x), intercept, R2 and the correlation, each labelled with its n, the ranges and the transform. R2 says how well one straight line fits the samples, not where they sit. x DEPTH gives the trend with depth in words; log_y fits log10(y) (e.g. permeability against porosity) and counts the samples a logarithm leaves out; e.g. RHOB on NPHI for the matrix line.
lag_correlation: Depth matching by cross-correlation: for each pair of the curves (2-5), the correlation at zero lag and its strongest value within +/- max_lag, with the apparent depth shift dz = z_a - z_b at that peak, over the interval or each zone asked for.
stats: Statistics of one or more curves over each zone and the zones pooled, one line per zone and curve, and the whole interval where samples outside the zones add to it, with what those samples hold (they are runs thinner than the zone minimum, not a zone). Each curve's label says what it is (measured, a model output of a step, a flag, a parameter) and what the record knows about it (uncalibrated beside a core-calibrated twin, a quicklook or fallback input, not computed here). With no statistics named: n of N, mean, median, P10, P90, min and max with their depths; a curve whose values are all positive and span more than two orders of magnitude also gets the geometric mean, its percentiles read on log10 values. Statistics you can name: n, mean, median, geo_mean, harmonic_mean, mode, min, max, range, std, variance, cv, iqr, or any percentile pNN. A curve of 0/1 values gives the share set, a curve of a few whole-number codes the share of each class (never a mean of codes). With where, only the samples where a condition holds (e.g. mean PHIE over NET_PAY).
runs: Where a condition holds, zone by zone: thickness and share of each zone, the total, the shallowest top and deepest base, and the runs top to base (every run up to limit, else the longest, with the get of every one); samples outside the zones apart, located. min_thickness and max_thickness keep only the runs at least or at most that thick (the thin beds alone: max_thickness); without them every run counts.
compare: Two curves where both have values: first the zone level (each zone's means: their rank correlation across the zones in words, and in how many zones a's mean is above b's), then each zone, the zones pooled, and the whole interval where samples outside the zones add to it: n of N, both means, the difference a - b and its spread (curves of one unit only), the share of samples with a > b and with a < b (beyond a tolerance when given), the rank correlation labelled with its n and the curves' ranges.
overlap: Where two conditions or classes hold together and apart (a and b: flags, section:CLASS, or CURVE OP VALUE terms): each zone from the top with the thickness and share of A, B, A and B, A without B and B without A; the zones where each holds; samples outside the zones apart; then the runs of A and B, of A without B and of B without A, top to base by zone. For asks that relate, align or coincide two indicators.
profile: One curve zone by zone from the top, then the zones pooled, and the whole interval where samples outside the zones add to it, with the statistics as stats gives them; the zones ranked by each statistic shown (the highest and the lowest), and each statistic's zone values against depth with the direction in words (higher upward or downward). A flag or class codes: their shares zone by zone, not ranked.
values_at: Curves read at depths: at each depth, the well's nearest sample (its depth and how far it lies from the depth asked, its zone, or the unit it lies in outside the interval) and each curve's value there, or that it has none; a range TOP-BASE lists every sample in it (up to 40). For a reading at a depth or a few samples; statistics over a stretch are stats.
section: One analyzer section as recorded: method, basis, and its classes as located runs: each class line starts with the class, then its criterion and its runs top to base zone by zone (every run when it has few, else the thickest, said so, with the runs call that lists every run), and its thickness and share on the line after.
step: One workflow step as recorded: method, inputs, the curves it wrote, equations, parameters, and the record's lines for this interval.
lithology_stats: Per rock type, then the zones pooled and the whole interval: the share of the zoned thickness and of the whole interval, and the curves' statistics (as stats gives them when none are named; a flag or class codes: their shares).
zone_contrast: What differs between the zones with higher and lower values of a curve: shale volume, porosity (or the inputs given) and lithology mix, thickness-weighted. Evidence for what controls a property.
curve_order: Whether curves keep an order (e.g. RSHA > RMED > RDEP), zone by zone and then sample by sample, in both directions.
threshold_exceedance: The share of samples beyond a threshold in each zone (and whether the zone's mean is beyond it), over the zones pooled and over the whole interval; the threshold you give, or the workflow policy's QC level for the curve, said which.
spike_flags: Outliers: samples beyond mean +/- k standard deviations of each zone's own values (baseline zone; zoned pools the zones, interval every sample); with k and baseline left out, the workflow's deviation rule (k 2 and 3 against each zone's own mean and std), said so; scale log10 screens log10 values; window N for a centred rolling median/MAD of N samples inside each zone. Each zone (its mean +/- std; a flagged zone with its bounds and largest samples: value, depth, zone, signed std), then the zones pooled and the whole interval; adjacent jumps.
adjacent_jumps: Changes between adjacent samples larger than a threshold in the curve's units (e.g. sonic cycle skips), in each zone, the zones pooled and the whole interval: the largest change, how many exceed it, and where.
vertical_sequence: Zones from base to top with the change of each curve from the zone below, grouped into packages of steps in one direction (cleaning- or dirtying-up).
pay_summary: Net rock, net reservoir and net pay: thickness, net-to-gross, the cutoffs, and the averages over the pay.
core_vs_log: Core plug statistics against the log values at the core depths, each with its n, in each zone with core samples, the zones pooled and the whole interval.
zone_classes: A topic's classes both ways: each zone's class from its mean values (an analyzer run on zone means) and the share of its samples in each class, then over the zones pooled and the whole interval.
formation_summary: For each curve and statistic (as stats gives them when none are named; a flag or class codes: the share of each class), the zones ranked high to low, the zones pooled and the whole interval; the lithology shares of the zoned thickness and of the gross; the zones in bad hole above the policy's confidence limit.
data_record: The workflow's data-completeness record per zone: primary logs missing, each measured log's share of samples with a value and its gaps, derived curves with no value and the inputs they lack.
unit_roles: The workflow's flow roles by permeability (Petrophys flow_roles on each zone's mean, with the policy's thresholds): its 'strongest' zone, the largest flow capacity (permeability-thickness) and possible baffles, with what qualifies each.
calculate: Recompute a property with Petrophys, with another method or other parameters (e.g. saturation with method simandoux; net_pay with sw_cutoff 0.5; porosity with matrix dolomite). Every input you leave out is the record's. Shows the change against the record's parameters, zones pooled and each zone, and writes the new curves as <CURVE>_<LABEL> (e.g. SW_SIMANDOUX), which every lookup and condition reads. An input another property computes (Rw, VCL, PHIE) is changed by calculating that property (water_resistivity with rw and rw_temp_f, clay_volume, porosity); the change carries into the steps that read it. With the property alone, lists its parameters with the record's values. Properties and their methods:
estimate: Estimate a parameter from this well's own logs with Petrophys, to set against the record's value it states: rw (rwa: apparent water resistivity over clean, porous samples, writes RWA; pickett; sp: from the SP log, needs Rmf), archie_m (pickett: a, m and n), clay_point (the shale's NPHI and RHOB), gr_endpoints (GR clean and shale as the clay-volume step picks them), matrix (apparent matrix density RHOMAA, and UMAA with PEF), temperature (formation temperature and gradient; a BHT refines it). zones limits the samples; vcl_max sets what is clean (0.3); phie_min what is porous (0.05). Parameters and methods:
what_if: An input's effect on a target: Petrophys recomputes for each value, every other input the record's. E.g. {"property": "net_pay", "parameter": "sw_cutoff", "values": [0.4, 0.5, 0.6]}; {"property": "saturation", "parameter": "model", "values": ["archie", "simandoux", "indonesia"]}; {"property": "saturation", "parameter": "m", "values": [1.8, 2.2], "target": "NET_PAY"}. target: a curve the property's step or the steps after it write (default: the property's main curve). Writes no curves; calculate the one you keep.
check: Check the data's quality with Petrophys: what is one of the objects below. Flags it finds are written as curves of this question (runs and stats read them); curves and zones narrow it. Objects:
classify: Classify the rock or its fluids with Petrophys: what is one of the objects below; method, curves and k where the object takes them. Classes are written as curves of this question. Objects:
summarize: Summarize reservoir quantities with Petrophys, each zone and the zones pooled: what is one of the objects below. Cutoffs are the record's unless given (vcl_cutoff, phie_cutoff, sw_cutoff). Objects:
calibrate: Set logs against core, or derive elastic properties, with Petrophys: what is one of the objects below. Core objects need a core curve in the well. Objects:
